propositions.text: This is an application for judicial review of a RAD decision dated April 8, 2019.
The RAD concluded the Applicant is neither a Convention refugee under section 96 IRPA nor a person in need of protection under section 97 IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court states this is a judicial review application of a RAD decision denying the Applicant refugee and protection status under IRPA.

propositions.text: The RAD confirmed the RPD's findings, especially that the Applicant had a viable Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) in Islamabad.
The RAD identified the IFA finding as determinative.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the RAD confirmed the RPD's finding of a viable IFA in Islamabad, which was determinative.

propositions.text: The RAD's discussion on the availability of a viable IFA was speculative about ongoing persecution threat.
The RAD's discussion was incomplete as it failed to assess the full range of factors under the second prong of the IFA test.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the RAD's IFA discussion was speculative and incomplete regarding the applicable test's second prong.

propositions.text: The RAD's decision was not unreasonable.
The application for judicial review is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the RAD decision was reasonable and dismisses the judicial review application.

propositions.text: The Applicant is a Pakistani citizen and drugstore owner in Sahiwal District, Punjab province.
The Applicant is a trained pharmacy technician licensed to sell drugs and narcotics.
The Applicant supplied free contraceptives to a nearby doctor.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant is a Pakistani citizen, drugstore owner, licensed pharmacy technician, and supplied free contraceptives locally.

propositions.text: On August 15, 2016, unknown gang members came to the Applicant's drugstore seeking bulk prescription medications.
One individual threatened to kill the Applicant and his family after refusal to supply medicine.

paragraphs.summary: The court recounts a threat by a gang to the Applicant and his family after he refused to supply bulk medications.

propositions.text: On September 9, 2016, the Applicant was kidnapped and tortured by the same gang in Punjab province.
The gang demanded medications; the Applicant escaped and filed a police report.

paragraphs.summary: The court describes the Applicant's kidnapping, torture, medication demands, escape, and police report filing.

propositions.text: On September 10 and 15, 2016, the Applicant was threatened by religious leaders and Taliban members to close his drugstore.
Threats included death threats to the Applicant and his immediate family due to contraceptive supply.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant was threatened by religious and Taliban figures to close his drugstore, with death threats.

propositions.text: The Applicant closed his drugstore on September 16, 2016, due to fear.
On September 18, 2016, the Applicant contacted police who apparently refused to investigate.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Applicant closed his drugstore and police refused to investigate his complaint.

propositions.text: The Applicant and family moved to Karachi, receiving threatening phone calls at his business number.
These calls confirmed his fear of persecution, leading him to leave Pakistan for Canada on October 20, 2016.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant moved to Karachi, received threats, and left Pakistan for Canada on October 20, 2016.

propositions.text: On November 30, 2016, the Applicant claimed refugee status, recounting threats and phone calls.
An affidavit from the Applicant's friend stated unknown persons searched for the Applicant in Sahiwal on January 7, 2017.

paragraphs.summary: The court records the Applicant's refugee claim and affidavit about persons searching for him in Sahiwal in 2017.

propositions.text: The refugee claim was transferred to the RPD, which held a hearing on June 15, 2017, and rejected the claim on June 30, 2017.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RPD held a hearing and rejected the Applicant's refugee claim in June 2017.

propositions.text: The court will set out the RPD decision in detail despite reviewing the RAD decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court decides to detail the RPD decision even though the review concerns the RAD decision.

propositions.text: The RPD found the Applicant's credibility determinative, noting omissions, contradictions, vagueness, and evasiveness.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the Applicant's credibility determinative, citing inconsistencies and evasiveness in testimony.

propositions.text: The RPD did not believe the Applicant was threatened as claimed or that incidents occurred as described.
The Applicant failed to prove on balance of probabilities he would face danger or risk under subsection 97(1) IRPA elsewhere in Pakistan.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD disbelieved the Applicant's threats and found he failed to prove risk of danger elsewhere in Pakistan.

propositions.text: Even if assaults and threats occurred, the Applicant had a viable IFA in Islamabad.
Threats arose from refusal to supply medication and contraceptive provision, but closure of drugstore ended risk.
No evidence suggested assailants would pursue the Applicant to Islamabad.
No evidence suggested difficulty travelling or settling in Islamabad; Applicant is successful and educated.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found a viable IFA in Islamabad since the risk ended with drugstore closure and no evidence of pursuit or settlement difficulty.

propositions.text: The Applicant appealed the RPD decision to the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the Applicant appealed the RPD decision to the RAD.

propositions.text: The Applicant argued the RPD erred in credibility and viable IFA findings in his RAD appeal.
The Applicant did not present new evidence or request a RAD hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argued RPD errors on credibility and IFA to the RAD without new evidence or hearing request.

propositions.text: The Applicant suggested the viable IFA determination was made in a factual vacuum or false premise.
The Applicant claimed evidence showed assailants could track him but gave no further details.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argued the IFA finding was flawed and assailants could track him, without elaboration.

propositions.text: The RAD found the only determinative issue was whether the RPD erred on the IFA evaluation.
The RAD found no error in the RPD's IFA assessment and dismissed the appeal.
The RAD found it unnecessary to discuss the Applicant's credibility issues.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found the IFA issue determinative, found no RPD error, dismissed the appeal, and did not address credibility.

propositions.text: Whether the RAD committed a reviewable error in finding Islamabad offers a viable IFA is the only issue argued by the Applicant.
The Applicant did not raise the issue of the RAD not ruling on the RPD's credibility finding.
The Applicant focused only on the RAD decision's finding on the viability of the IFA, making credibility discussion unnecessary.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues only that the RAD erred in finding Islamabad a viable IFA and did not raise the RPD credibility issue; the court states this is the sole issue.

propositions.text: Suggests RAD should address RPD credibility findings in future to avoid unreasonable IFA analyses and remands.

paragraphs.summary: The court suggests RAD should address RPD credibility findings in future to avoid remands due to incomplete IFA analyses.

propositions.text: Vavilov sets a presumption of reasonableness standard of review unless rebutted by clear legislative intent or rule of law exceptions.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains Vavilov's framework presuming reasonableness standard of review unless exceptions apply.

propositions.text: Applicant argues correctness standard applies because RAD violated natural justice and misapplied the viable IFA test, raising general legal questions.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the correctness standard applies due to RAD's natural justice violation and improper IFA test application.

propositions.text: The RAD identified and followed the appropriate test for viable IFA determination.
Issues do not engage questions of central legal importance but concern specific issues affecting the Applicant.
No procedural fairness breach by RAD is found.
The issue of IFA availability is within RAD's delegated authority and must be reviewed on a reasonableness standard.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RAD applied the correct test, no procedural fairness breach, and reasonableness standard applies to IFA issues.

propositions.text: IFA question is essential to refugee system and ensures international refugee law backs national protection when inadequate.
IFA concept is supported by case law, textbooks, and UNHCR guidelines.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the IFA concept is essential to refugee law and supported by case law and UNHCR guidelines.

propositions.text: IFA ensures persecuted individuals seek protection within their country before international refugee system (Ward case).

paragraphs.summary: The court explains IFA ensures refugees seek protection internally before international refugee protection, citing Ward.

propositions.text: RAD found Applicant safe in Islamabad with no evidence of persecution agents pursuing him there and ability to earn a living.
RAD confirmed RPD's conclusion that an IFA was available to the Applicant based on these factors.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found Islamabad safe and viable as an IFA, confirming the RPD's conclusion.

propositions.text: Two-prong IFA test requires no serious possibility of persecution and unreasonableness of seeking refuge there (Rasaratnam, Thirunavukkarasu).
Both prongs must be satisfied for IFA finding; supported by other cases.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the two-prong IFA test requires no serious persecution risk and reasonableness of seeking refuge, both must be met.

propositions.text: Both prongs ensure Canada complies with international norms on IFAs (UNHCR Guidelines).

paragraphs.summary: The court notes the two-prong IFA test ensures compliance with international norms per UNHCR guidelines.

propositions.text: Gallo Farias checklist clarifies IFA legal criteria including notice, two-step test, burden of proof, high threshold for unreasonableness, accessibility, and lack of friends/relatives not determinative.

paragraphs.summary: The court summarizes Gallo Farias checklist clarifying IFA criteria including notice, burden, test, accessibility, and reasonableness.

propositions.text: Applicant submits RAD erred on both prongs of the Rasaratnam-Thirunavukkarasu IFA test.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the RAD erred on both prongs of the IFA test.

propositions.text: Applicant argues RAD erred by speculating risk ceased yet finding viable IFA, which is inconsistent.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues RAD's finding of no risk but viable IFA is inconsistent speculation and error.

propositions.text: Court rejects Applicant's argument, finding RAD analyzed risk and concluded no persecution risk in Pakistan.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the Applicant's argument, finding RAD concluded no persecution risk in Pakistan.

propositions.text: RAD stated that even if assault and threat occurred, claim would be rejected due to IFA in Islamabad.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD stated that even if threats occurred, the claim would be rejected due to Islamabad IFA.

propositions.text: RAD did not speculate but assumed risk for IFA determination, which is acceptable and not inconsistent.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RAD assumed risk for IFA analysis without speculation, which is acceptable and consistent.

propositions.text: Applicant argues RAD's finding of Islamabad as IFA was a 'knee jerk' reaction without analysis.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues RAD's Islamabad IFA finding was a 'knee jerk' reaction lacking analysis.

propositions.text: Applicant was given full opportunity to challenge Islamabad as IFA per Gallo Farias.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Applicant had full opportunity to challenge Islamabad as IFA.

propositions.text: RPD identified Islamabad as acceptable IFA where Applicant would not face persecution risk.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD identified Islamabad as an acceptable IFA where Applicant would not face persecution risk.

propositions.text: Applicant said he left Karachi due to fear but did not specifically say if he could live in Islamabad, claiming countrywide threat.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant said he left Karachi fearing persecution but did not specify if he could live in Islamabad, citing countrywide threat.

propositions.text: Threatening calls in Karachi and friend's affidavit show continued risk of persecution even in Islamabad

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues threatening calls and a friend's affidavit show continued persecution risk even in Islamabad.

propositions.text: Pakistani police may be corrupt and leak Applicant's location, undermining IFA viability

paragraphs.summary: Applicant's counsel argues police corruption risks leaks, undermining IFA viability.

propositions.text: RAD found persecutors uninterested in Islamabad due to closed drugstore and lack of evidence of intent to find Applicant there

paragraphs.summary: RAD found persecutors uninterested in Islamabad due to closed drugstore and no evidence of intent to find Applicant there.

propositions.text: RAD found Applicant could avoid threatening calls by changing phone number and no evidence of assailants' location or knowledge of Applicant in Karachi

paragraphs.summary: RAD found Applicant could avoid calls by changing number and no evidence assailants knew Applicant's Karachi location.

propositions.text: RAD found assailants unaware of Applicant's whereabouts and lack of threats to family shows little interest in targeting Applicant
Mere suspicions of being hunted insufficient to preclude acceptable IFA (Kumar v Canada, 2012 FC 30)

paragraphs.summary: RAD found assailants unaware of Applicant's location and little interest in targeting; mere suspicions insufficient to preclude IFA (Kumar).

propositions.text: RAD ruled Applicant failed to show relocation to IFA would pose unacceptable risk
Burden of proof on Applicant to show risk (Gallo Farias, Thirunavukkarasu, Mwaura, Whenu)

paragraphs.summary: RAD ruled Applicant failed burden to show IFA relocation risk, citing relevant authorities.

propositions.text: RAD found insufficient evidence of persecution risk in Islamabad
Court finds RAD's findings reasonable and will not disturb determination under first prong of Rasaratnam-Thironavukkarasu test

paragraphs.summary: RAD found insufficient persecution risk evidence; Court finds RAD's findings reasonable under first prong test.

propositions.text: RAD's second prong analysis incomplete, failing to address full range of issues for seeking refuge in Islamabad

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD's second prong analysis incomplete, missing full range of issues for refuge in Islamabad.

propositions.text: RAD only considered business prospects, should have addressed transportation, language, education, accommodation, religion, indigenous status, healthcare
Applicant cites RAD case lacking legal basis for enumerated factors, claims unjustified omission

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues RAD only considered business prospects, omitting other factors, citing unsupported RAD case.

propositions.text: RAD claimed Applicant did not contest RPD's second prong analysis
Applicant says RAD misconstrued appeal memorandum, which challenges RPD's lack of state protection analysis in Islamabad

paragraphs.summary: RAD said Applicant did not contest second prong; Applicant says RAD misconstrued memorandum challenging state protection analysis.

propositions.text: Respondent agrees RAD was correct to not address each factor as second prong was uncontested
Applicant provided no evidence showing RAD's second prong determination was unreasonable

paragraphs.summary: Respondent agrees RAD need not address each factor as second prong uncontested; Applicant gave no evidence of unreasonableness.

propositions.text: Court rejects Applicant's arguments for four reasons

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects Applicant's arguments for four reasons.

propositions.text: Applicant did not raise 'range of issues' argument at RAD level despite burden of proof
Applicant only challenged RPD's state protection analysis, relating to first prong

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Applicant did not raise 'range of issues' at RAD and only challenged state protection analysis related to first prong.

propositions.text: Applicant's RAD memorandum omits factors like transportation, language, education, accommodation, religion, indigenous status, healthcare
Raising new legal issues at judicial review barred (Alberta Teachers' Association, Forest Ethics, Erasmo)

paragraphs.summary: Applicant's RAD memorandum omits key factors; raising new legal issues at review barred by precedent.

propositions.text: Second prong's 'reasonable in all circumstances' standard is high, fact-specific, requiring concrete evidence (Ranganathan, Thirunavukkarasu)
Applicant's argument would improperly confine inquiry and shift burden to tribunal, frustrating case-by-case test

paragraphs.summary: Court explains second prong standard is high and fact-specific; Applicant's argument would improperly constrain inquiry and shift burden.

propositions.text: Applicant provided no evidence or substantive argument on Islamabad's adequacy for employment, shelter, services
Applicant faults RAD for not investigating suitability, but burden lies with Applicant to show undue hardship (Okonkwo)

paragraphs.summary: Applicant gave no evidence on Islamabad's adequacy and wrongly faults RAD; burden to show hardship lies with Applicant.

propositions.text: Court's role in judicial review is not to reweigh evidence under second prong (Vavilov, Akinfolajimi, Titcombe, Khosa)
Applicant essentially asks Court to reweigh evidence, which is improper

paragraphs.summary: Court states judicial review does not allow reweighing evidence; Applicant improperly asks for this.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review is dismissed
No question for certification

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses judicial review application and finds no question for certification.
